messages:
maya: quick follow-up from the onboarding pipeline RFC — noticed some edge cases when running the nightly bench sweep.
alex: which edge cases? saw a spike on Llama-2-70b-nf in ort-quant jobs yesterday.
maya: yeah, two categories: (1) shape/prompt-length regressions causing OOM in the runtime despite passing unit smoke, (2) conversion artifacts for models with custom ops (xformers variants) that our ONNX export silently fakes -> perf hits.
kevin: for (1) are these long-tail seq-len inputs or weird batch combos? we thought auto-batching + prefix cache would handle.
maya: mostly long-tail: seqs >2048 with lots of short prefixes queued behind a one big request. Batch packing makes kernel selection pick a less optimal path.
jonathan: hmm. could we add a 'max_effective_seq' fingerprint as part of the model metadata and use it to refuse or flag model until runtime supports >N? then boot a compatible kernel selection in dedicated.
sam: +1. also thinking we need a synthetic bench that exercises multi-epoch mixing: do short+long combos to catch kernel degenerations.
alex: implementing that synthetic bench would help. but tradeoff: noise vs signal. we should keep a stable baseline seed and a deterministic input sampler. otherwise CI flakes.
maya: agreed. prototype config we used:
```
bench_profile:
  name: longtail_mixed
  seed: 1729
  mix:
    - {len: 64, pct: 0.6}
    - {len: 4096, pct: 0.3}
    - {len: 8192, pct: 0.1}
```
kevin: for (2) custom ops — proposal: on model ingest, run a light ONNX validation that enumerates ops and matches against our verified-oplist; if unknown, mark as `needs-adapter` and run a compatibility job that attempts a fallback kernel and records perf delta.
jonathan: and we should record that delta in the model registry as 'compat_score' and surface it in console. customers can opt to accept lower perf or request conversion assistance.
build-bot: deploy pipeline/ingest v0.9.3 started for model 'llama-2-70b-custom' — job 8721
sam: another corner: quantized checkpoints that have per-channel vs per-tensor scales; conversions sometimes normalize incorrectly. failing tests are subtle — logits diffs small but decode quality drops.
alex: we need a small eval set (30 prompts) that detects decode-quality change, not just token-l2. maybe use MRR on synthetic QA and a small human-reviewed pass.
maya: yes. add "semantic_regression" stage to admit pipeline: run quick eval, threshold on BLEU/MRR/QA-acc. If fail, mark `admit:hold` and attach failure artifacts.
kevin: operational decision: do we fail onboarding or keep model in 'warmed' but non-default routing? prefer soft-fail: auto-route to a fall-back model with a note to the user.
jonathan: we should also add an expirable cache for 'bench variants' to avoid constant rebenching for tiny commits. TTL 24h by default.
sam: action items:
- maya: add longtail_mixed bench profile + deterministic sampler
- alex: add semantic_regression harness + metrics spec
- kevin: implement op-enumeration + compat_score in registry
- jonathan: add routing policy flag `fail_open` default true
maya: I'll PR the bench profile and update the onboarding RFC with the soft-fail flow. anyone want to pair on the compat_score schema?
alex: i'll pair tmrw 10am PT
maya: cool. tagging: @kevin @jonathan
kevin: noted. one more: we should log kernel-selection decisions in trace-level runtime logs to correlate perf regressions.
jonathan: agree. add a lightweight telemetry sample (1%) to avoid too much volume.
maya: thanks all. will open threads for each action with small specs.
build-bot: ingest v0.9.3 job 8721 completed: success
